successors.note: Cliopatria's Greenland row stops in 1940 and its Denmark row carries Greenland only from 1946 (the 1945 Denmark shape excludes it); this dossier keeps the colony to 1953, the year the pages give for the end of colonial status.

capitals.name: Godthåb (Nuuk)
capitals.note: 'The colony was centred at Godthåb' (Greenland page); the settlement of Nuuk, then called Godthåb, dates from 1728. During 1940-45 Greenland governed itself from Nuuk under its two sheriffs (Greenland in World War II page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Greenland shape begins in 1734 but the colonization began in 1721 ('Hans Egede received a royal charter' in 1721 and later 'established Hope Colony on Kangeq'; Greenland infobox 'Danish-Norwegian resettlement and colonization: 1721'). The page gives no separate year for the Hope Colony, so the 1721-1733 core is the Nuuk district only; the royal colony at Godthåb dates from 1728 and its retinue was recalled in 1730.

correction.text: Hope Colony on Kangeq and, from 1728, the settlement of Godthåb (Nuuk): the first Danish-Norwegian foothold on the south-west coast

keyframe_review.note: 10,964 km2: a thin coastal strip from the Nuuk district (64.2N) to Christianshåb (68.8N), which the page dates 1734. The infobox area (2,166,086 km2) is the whole island and is not comparable with a colonial coast strip (ratio 0.005); the shape is read as 'the colonized coast', not as sovereign area.

Kept as drawn.
11,874 km2: both Jacobshavn cells are back; Colonial Greenland lists 'Jacobshavn (1741)'.

41,085 km2: 94 cells added between 62.0N and 65.5N (the coast south of Nuuk down to Frederikshåb and a little to the north of Nuuk), i.e. the Frederikshåb district; the page dates Frederikshåb to 1742 (shape two years later) and Fiskenæs, on the same stretch, to 1754. 103,429 km2: two cells added at 70.1N; no page event, a boundary refinement of about 500 km2 under the grid's resolution. The page lists no foundation between 1797 and 1894.
103,713 km2: the same cells; no event, no border move.
104,134 km2: one cell at 72.3N added; no page event, a refinement under the grid's resolution.

105,297 km2: three cells appear at 65.6-65.8N, 37.6-37.9W, the Ammassalik coast on the east side. The Tasiilaq page dates the Holm expedition to 1884-1885 ('marking the area's first connections with Europe') but the 'permanent settlement was founded in 1894 as a Danish trading station', and Colonial Greenland agrees ('until the establishment of Amassalik on the eastern shore in 1894'), so the east coast is drawn nine years early.

correction.text: the 1885 shape without the Ammassalik coast until the 1894 station (the shape holds 1885-1894; the east-coast cells return in 1894)

keyframe_review.note: 105,748 km2: Ammassalik (1894) is inside; one more cell at 72.4N (a refinement). Nothing else on the pages for 1895-1907.
107,279 km2: four detached cells appear at the far north-east and north-west (76.9-78.5N, 18.7W to 72.4W). None of the nine pages explains them (unverified: page budget).

156,960 km2 (+50,000): 137 cells added between 68.3N and 78.2N, 50.1W to 72.0W, 57 of them within 150 km of Qaanaaq. The Qaanaaq page dates 'a missionary and trading post at North Star Bay' set up by Knud Rasmussen and Peter Freuchen to 1910, but says 'Denmark assumed control of the village in 1937' and 'the United States abandoned its territorial claims in the area in 1917'. Cliopatria therefore draws the north-west coast as Danish 26 years before the page's Danish control: kept as drawn, flagged soft and left to a gap-filler.

159,055 km2: six cells on the east coast at 65.9-66.2N north of Ammassalik; no page event (unverified: page silent). The History page records that after the 1917 sale of the Virgin Islands the United States 'agreed to give up its claims on Greenland'.
160,191 km2: five more cells on the east coast at 66.0-66.3N; no page event (unverified: page silent).
169,530 km2 (+9,300): 28 cells added at 69.4-70.3N, 52-55W (the Disko Island area); no page event (unverified: page budget). Scoresbysund (the page's 1925) is not in this shape.

The shape is listed to 1935 but Erik the Red's Land (the east coast between 71.5N and 75.7N) was Norwegian-occupied from 1931 and awarded to Denmark on 5 April 1933, so this shape holds 1926-1932 and the next keyframe takes over. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1926..1932 from this entry's own 'valid 1926-1932 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

Cliopatria's Kingdom of Norway 1932-1935 shape holds that zone ('Greenland' among its countries), so it is used to name the zone. keyframe_review.note: 2,219,796 km2: the whole island, against the infobox's 2,166,086 km2 (ratio 1.02). No page dates anything in 1936; the pages give the Danish claim to all of Greenland at the 1919 peace conference (Eastern Greenland Case page) and the 1933 award, and Qaanaaq's 1937 Danish control of the village. Kept as drawn; the 1936 date is Cliopatria's.
1940 only: the same whole-island shape. On 9 April 1940 Denmark fell to Germany and Greenland became 'an unoccupied territory of an occupied nation'.

New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Greenland row after 1940; its USA row draws the whole island as plain US land in 1941-1945 (the US dossier removes it and records the protection as a tint) and its Denmark row (1945) excludes it. Greenland stayed under Danish sovereignty, governed by its sheriffs, and from 9 April 1941 became 'a protected state of the United States' under the Kauffmann-Hull agreement (the Greenland page dates the American occupation to 8 April 1941).

correction.text: unchanged whole-island shape, the status changing to American protection

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Greenland Administration 'again came under direct control from Copenhagen' after the 5 May 1945 liberation (the page gives no day); the colony lasted until 1953 ('In 1953, Greenland's colonial status was ended', Colonial Greenland). Cliopatria's Denmark row also contains Greenland from 1946, so the compile step must let one of the two win for 1946-1953.

ledger.note: 1721: Hans Egede's Dano-Norwegian expedition begins the colonization of Greenland at Hope Colony on Kangeq. 'Hans Egede received a royal charter' in 1721 and 'later established Hope Colony on Kangeq' (Colonial Greenland, which gives no year for the colony itself); History of Greenland: 'In 1721, aspiring to become a colonial power, Denmark-Norway sent a missionary expedition to Greenland'; the Greenland infobox: 'Danish-Norwegian resettlement and colonization: 1721'. Kangeq is placed by Nuuk.

region.text: Hope Colony on Kangeq, in the Nuuk district

ledger.note: 1721: Greenland is a colony of Denmark-Norway. The Greenland infobox gives 'Danish-Norwegian resettlement and colonization: 1721' and History of Greenland says Denmark-Norway sent the expedition; the dependency is drawn as the metropole's tint (mirror of the crown's side, as in other colony dossiers); the Danish-Norwegian crown's own dossier draws no Greenland land.

region.text: Hope Colony on Kangeq and the Nuuk district

ledger.note: 1728: the royal colony is founded at Godthåb (Nuuk). A royal colony under Major Claus Paarss 'established the settlement of Nuuk, then called Godthåb ("Good Hope"), in 1728'; Colonial Greenland adds that this settlement 'failed due to mutiny' and its retinue was recalled in 1730. 'Capital' is the researcher's reading: the Greenland page says 'The colony was centred at Godthåb'.

1734: the colony reaches Christianshåb (Qasigiannguit). The page lists 'Christianshåb (1734)' among the settlements founded 1734-1774 under the General Trade Company; Cliopatria's first shape (1734) is the coast from Godthåb to Christianshåb. The radius is the researcher's reading of the colony's district.

1738: Severin's monopoly trade reaches Jacobshavn and the Dutch are repulsed. The History page has Severin 'successfully repulsed the Dutch at the Battle of Jacobshavn' in 1738-1739 but says nothing of a founding or of land; Cliopatria draws the Jacobshavn coast from 1738 and Colonial Greenland dates the colony to 1741 (bridging at confidence 1).
1741: Jacobshavn (Ilulissat) is founded. The page lists 'Jacobshavn (1741)'.
1742: Frederikshåb (Paamiut) is founded. The page lists 'Frederikshåb (1742)'; Cliopatria's shape for the coast south of Nuuk begins in 1744.
1752: Claushavn is founded. The page lists 'Claushavn (1752)'; the modern name is not on the page and Claushavn is placed within 60 km of the nearest gazetteer town, Ilulissat.
1754: Fiskenæs is founded. The page lists 'Fiskenæs (1754)'; the place is named by its Greenlandic name, Qeqertarsuatsiaat, which the gazetteer lacks.

1755: Ritenbenck, Egedesminde and Sukkertoppen are founded. The page lists 'Ritenbenck, Egedesminde and Sukkertoppen (1755)'; they are placed at Saqqaq, Aasiaat and Maniitsoq, names the gazetteer lacks.
1756: Holstensborg (Sisimiut) is founded. The page lists 'Holstensborg (1756)'.
1758: Umanak (Uummannaq) is founded. The page lists 'Umanak (1758)'; Cliopatria draws it only from 1778 and the keyframe reviews add it from 1758.
1769: the districts between the 1750s colonies are filled in (confidence 1). Cliopatria's 1769 shape adds 45 cells between 63.0N and 69.5N; none of the pages opened dates a 1769 event.

region.text: the cells Cliopatria adds in 1769 between 63.0N and 69.5N

ledger.note: 1771: Upernavik is founded. The page lists 'Upernavik (1771)'; Cliopatria draws its latitude only from 1805.
1773: Godhavn is founded on Disko Island. The page lists 'Godhavn (1773)'.

1774: Julianehaab (Qaqortoq) is founded and the Royal Greenland Trade Department replaces the General Trade Company. The page lists 'Julianehaab (1774)'; Cliopatria's shape reaches the southern tip in 1772.

1788: Cliopatria adds 74 cells between 61.3N and 64.3N (confidence 1: bridging). None of the pages dates anything that year; the 1782 Instructions the page mentions set up separate councils for North and South Greenland, which is administration.

region.text: the cells Cliopatria adds in 1788 between 61.3N and 64.3N

ledger.note: 1797: Nennortalik, the last settlement for a century, is founded. The page says 'construction of new settlements was effectively suspended after' Nennortalik (1797).

14 January 1814: the Treaty of Kiel leaves Greenland with Denmark when Norway is ceded; the colony passes from Denmark-Norway to the Kingdom of Denmark. 'When the union between the crowns of Denmark and Norway was dissolved in 1814, the Treaty of Kiel severed Norway's former colonies'; History of Greenland: 'The colonies, including Greenland, remained in Danish possession.' The day is the Greenland infobox's 'Unification with Denmark: 14 January 1814'. No land changes: the metropole is denmark-norway to this date and kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940 (Cliopatria's Denmark-Norway row 1814-1940) afterwards.

14 January 1814: the colony's metropole, the union of Denmark and Norway, ends. 'When the union between the crowns of Denmark and Norway was dissolved in 1814, the Treaty of Kiel severed Norway's former colonies'; Greenland stayed with Denmark (the next event).

region.text: the colony as Cliopatria draws it in 1814

ledger.note: 14 January 1814: Greenland remains a Danish colony under the Kingdom of Denmark. 'The colonies, including Greenland, remained in Danish possession.' The slug is that of Cliopatria's Denmark-Norway row for 1814-1940, which the Danish dossier splits off.

region.text: the colony as Cliopatria draws it in 1814

ledger.note: 1894: a Danish trading station is founded at Ammassalik (Tasiilaq) on the east coast. 'permanent settlement was founded in 1894 as a Danish trading station' (Tasiilaq; Colonial Greenland: 'until the establishment of Amassalik on the eastern shore in 1894').
1908: four detached cells appear at the far north (confidence 1: bridging). Cliopatria's 1908 shape adds them at 76.9-78.5N, 18.7W to 72.4W; none of the nine pages dates anything there.

region.text: the four cells Cliopatria adds in 1908

ledger.note: 1910: Knud Rasmussen and Peter Freuchen set up a trading post at North Star Bay (Thule). 'In 1910 explorers Knud Rasmussen and Peter Freuchen established a missionary and trading post at North Star Bay.' The page does not say the land became Danish: the United States gave up its claims in 1917 and 'Denmark assumed control of the village in 1937'; Cliopatria's 1911 shape draws the north-west coast as Danish (confidence 1).

region.text: the north-west coast Cliopatria adds in 1911, 57 of its cells within 150 km of Qaanaaq

ledger.note: 1917: the United States gives up its territorial claims in the Thule area. 'The United States abandoned its territorial claims in the area in 1917' (Qaanaaq); History of Greenland: after the sale of the Virgin Islands the United States 'agreed to give up its claims on Greenland'. A claim given up, not land held; counterpart nobody (reviewer eu-14-i, 2026-10-25): the United States held no land in Greenland in 1917 and its dossier records no loss here, and the Thule coast is already gained in 1910.

1925: Ejnar Mikkelsen founds Scoresbysund (Ittoqqortoormiit) on the east coast. 'Ittoqqortoormiit was founded in 1925 by Ejnar Mikkelsen and some 80 Inuit settlers'; 'The settlement was encouraged by the colonial power'. Cliopatria's shape adds its cells in 1926.

June-July 1931: Norway occupies Erik the Red's Land on the east coast. 'June 1931: Hallvard Devold raised the Norwegian flag at Myggbukta'; on 10 July 1931 a Norwegian royal proclamation claimed the coast 'between Carlsberg Fjord in the South and Bessel Fjord in the North' (71 deg 30' to 75 deg 40'N), its western limit assumed to be the Inland Ice. The zone is named by Cliopatria's Norway shape of 1932.

region.text: Erik the Red's Land, Carlsberg Fjord to Bessel Fjord, 71 deg 30' to 75 deg 40'N

ledger.note: 5 April 1933: the Permanent Court of International Justice rules against Norway and awards the east coast to Denmark. The infobox gives '5 April 1933' for the territory awarded to Denmark and the page says Norway abandoned its claim in 1933; the Eastern Greenland Case page's reference gives 5 September 1933 for the judgment.

region.text: Erik the Red's Land, awarded to Denmark

ledger.note: 1933: the east-coast zone passes to Denmark. The territory is the winner's in full colour from this year; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Norway row keeps this zone until 1935, which the Norway dossier's owner should cut.

region.text: Erik the Red's Land, awarded to Denmark

ledger.note: 1936: the whole island is drawn as Greenland (confidence 1: Cliopatria's date). The Eastern Greenland Case page records Denmark's 1919 claim to 'the whole of Greenland' and the Court's award of 'the disputed territory' only; no page opened dates 1936.

region.text: the interior ice sheet and the uncolonized north and east coasts, drawn by Cliopatria as Greenland from 1936

ledger.note: 9 April 1940: with Denmark occupied by Germany, Greenland governs itself. The colony becomes 'an unoccupied territory of an occupied nation'; the sheriffs Eske Brun (South) and Aksel Svane (North) declared self-rule 'invoking the emergency clause of a 1925 law'; the Greenland page: 'Greenland's connection to Denmark was severed on 9 April 1940'. Sovereignty is still Danish; no land changes.
9 April 1940: Greenland's tie to occupied Denmark is cut. 'Greenland's connection to Denmark was severed on 9 April 1940'; the colony governs itself until the American protection of April 1941.

9 April 1941: Greenland becomes a protected state of the United States. Henrik Kauffmann, against his government's instructions, 'signed an executive agreement with Secretary of State Cordell Hull' that made Greenland 'a protected state of the United States' and allowed American troops; the Greenland page says the United States 'occupied Greenland' on 8 April 1941.

region.text: Greenland, protected by the United States

ledger.note: 1945: Danish rule from Copenhagen resumes and the American protection ends. After the 5 May 1945 liberation the Greenland Administration under Brun 'surrendered its emergency powers' and 'again came under direct control from Copenhagen' (no day given); the Kauffmann-Hull agreement was replaced by a base treaty only in 1951, so the end of the protection in 1945 is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Greenland, back under direct Danish control

ledger.note: 1945: Greenland is again a Danish colony ruled from Copenhagen. After the 5 May 1945 liberation the Greenland Administration 'again came under direct control from Copenhagen' (no day given); the Denmark row of Cliopatria carries the island only from 1946.
1953: the colony's dependency on Denmark ends as Greenland becomes part of the Danish Realm. 'In 1953, Greenland's colonial status was ended' (Colonial Greenland).

1953: Greenland's colonial status ends and it becomes part of the Kingdom of Denmark. 'In 1953, Greenland's colonial status was ended' (Colonial Greenland); 'With the 1953 Danish constitution, Greenland's colonial status ended' (Greenland page); the History page says Greenland was raised from colony to an autonomous province or constituent country of the Danish Realm.

region.text: the whole island, now part of the Danish Realm

wars.name: Battle of Jacobshavn
wars.outcome: The monopoly holder Jacob Severin 'successfully repulsed the Dutch at the Battle of Jacobshavn'; no change of land is recorded.
wars.note: Skirmishes over trade at Jacobshavn, 1738-1739; Colonial Greenland dates the colony to 1741.

wars.name: Eastern Greenland case (Norwegian occupation of Erik the Red's Land)

zones.text: Erik the Red's Land, 71 deg 30' to 75 deg 40'N

wars.outcome: Norway occupied the east coast in 1931 and proclaimed it Norwegian on 10 July; the Permanent Court of International Justice ruled against Norway and awarded the disputed territory to Denmark (5 April 1933), after which Norway abandoned its claim.
wars.note: A legal dispute with stations on the ground (Myggbukta, Jonsbu, Antarctic Havn), not a shooting war. The Eastern Greenland Case page's reference gives 5 September 1933 for the judgment.

wars.name: German weather stations on East Greenland (Second World War)
wars.outcome: The Germans set up four clandestine weather stations on the east coast from August 1942; the Sledge Patrol and American forces attacked or captured them (Holzauge found 11 March 1943, Bassgeiger attacked 22 April 1944, Edelweiss II captured 4 November 1944); no territory changed hands.
wars.note: Also in 1940 the Royal Navy demolished the Norwegian stations on the east coast, drawing an American protest.

certainty.note: A colony of settlements and trading districts along the south-west and west coast, later two spots on the east coast; no survey lines. The districts are drawn as coast strips and the interior was no one's. The east-coast zone is a treaty-less claim until the 1933 judgment.

The island's coast is the frontier. Sovereignty over the Thule district is the one open question (Denmark 'assumed control of the village in 1937'); the sea boundary with Canada across Nares Strait is not drawn on land.

notes:
Greenland (Cliopatria 'Greenland', 1734-1940, 24 shapes) is read as the Danish colony, type colony. Dossier life 1721-1953: 1721 is the page's colonization date (Cliopatria begins 1734); 1953 is the end of colonial status (Cliopatria's row stops in 1940 and Denmark's row has Greenland from 1946).

Pages: nine opened of a nine-page budget (Greenland, History of Greenland, Colonial Greenland, Erik the Red's Land, Eastern Greenland Case, Tasiilaq, Ittoqqortoormiit, Qaanaaq, Greenland in World War II). Wikipedia URLs that did not load: Legal_Status_of_Eastern_Greenland_case, Legal_Status_of_Eastern_Greenland, Legal_status_of_Eastern_Greenland, Erik_the_Red's_Land (unencoded apostrophe). The Treaty of Kiel, the Danmark Expedition, Hans Egede and the Royal Greenland Trading Department were not opened (budget).

Shape-by-shape: the colonies' founding years come from Colonial Greenland and all radii (25-60 km) are the researcher's reading of 'district'; Claushavn, Ritenbenck and Fiskenæs are placed from nearby towns. Adjusts: Umanak (page 1758, Cliopatria 1778) and Upernavik (1771, Cliopatria 1805) are added to the shapes that lack them; the Ammassalik cells are cut from 1885-1893 (station 1894). Unexplained Cliopatria steps, recorded at confidence 1: 1738 (two-cell shift), 1769 (+45 cells), 1788 (+74 cells), 1908 (four detached cells), 1911 (the north-west coast, Thule), 1915/1922 (east coast 66N, not given events), 1924 (+28 cells, north Disko Island, not given an event). Tiny refinements of 1-2 cells in 1805, 1830, 1856, 1895 have no events.

Open question: Thule. Cliopatria draws the north-west coast to Qaanaaq as Greenland from 1911; the Qaanaaq page has a private trading post in 1910, the US giving up its claims in 1917 and 'Denmark assumed control of the village in 1937'. A gap-filler should open the Thule Trading Station / Knud Rasmussen pages.

Overlaps to settle at compile time: (1) Cliopatria's Kingdom of Norway 1932-1935 shape contains Erik the Red's Land (about 33,000 km2 of Greenland) although Norway lost it in April 1933: the Norway dossier's owner should cut it at 1933; (2) Cliopatria's Denmark row contains Greenland from 1946, overlapping this dossier's 1946-1953 keyframe; (3) Cliopatria Canada's 1936-1940 neighbour listing for Greenland is the Nares Strait coast, not a land border: no event and no Hans Island page was opened.

Judgment dates disagree: Erik the Red's Land gives 5 April 1933 (twice); the Eastern Greenland Case page's reference gives 5 September 1933. The Greenland page dates the American occupation to 8 April 1941 and Greenland in World War II dates the Kauffmann-Hull agreement to 9 April 1941. Colonial Greenland lists Jacobshavn 1741; History of Greenland has the Dutch battle there in 1738-1739.

Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: Maniitsoq (Sukkertoppen), Aasiaat (Egedesminde), Saqqaq (Ritenbenck), Qeqertarsuatsiaat (Fiskenæs), Nanortalik (Nennortalik). Norse Greenland (Cliopatria row 1072-1384, another group) ends three centuries before this dossier begins; no predecessor is claimed. Metropole: Denmark-Norway (slug denmark-norway) to 14 January 1814, then the Kingdom of Denmark (slug kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940, to April 1940), then denmark from 1945; the colony is linked to each by a vassal_start/vassal_end pair (the colony's side of the tint, as in aden-protectorate), and the 1814 rename marks the change. The USA dossier carries the mirror of the 1941-1945 protection (vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart greenland); Cliopatria's USA row draws the whole island as US land in those years. Rulers: none documented on the pages opened; the key is omitted.
